title: Newark 1031 Exchange Coordination
name: Newark 1031 Exchange Coordination
metaTitle: Newark 1031 Exchange Coordination | San Jose, CA
metaDescription: 1031 exchange coordination for Newark single-tenant tech campuses, Dumbarton corridor industrial, and Cherry Street distribution buildings near Fremont.

sections.html: Newark sits at the base of the Dumbarton Bridge, and that position on the bridge corridor connecting the Peninsula to the East Bay has drawn a single-tenant tech campus, ordinary industrial buildings, and a residential edge around Ardenwood into one small city's commercial base. An exchanger identifying Newark replacement property is often looking at a single-tenant net-lease building rather than a multi-tenant property, which changes both the underwriting approach and the diligence checklist compared with the rest of the South Bay. Newark's commercial footprint is smaller in total square footage than Fremont's directly to the south, and much of what does exist here traces back to a handful of large parcels assembled decades ago rather than the incremental infill development seen in more built-out parts of the county.

sections.heading: The Dumbarton Corridor and Single-Tenant Tech Campuses
sections.html: The large single-tenant campus built on the former Sun Microsystems site near the Dumbarton corridor illustrates how Newark's commercial market can pivot around one anchor tenant more than in cities with a deeper multi-tenant office base. A buyer identifying single-tenant NNN property in Newark should review the tenant's corporate credit and lease term as closely as the building itself, since the entire income stream depends on that one tenant's continued occupancy rather than a diversified rent roll spread across many leases. Building specifications on a large single-tenant campus are also often customized to that original tenant's operations, so a buyer should think through re-leasing risk realistically, including the cost of reconfiguring the space for a different type of tenant if the current occupant were ever to vacate at lease expiration.

sections.heading: Industrial Space Along Cherry Street and Newark Boulevard
sections.html: Industrial buildings along Cherry Street and Newark Boulevard serve a mix of light manufacturing and distribution tenants supporting both local employers and the broader East Bay logistics network. Lease structures here vary between long-term single-tenant industrial and shorter flex space serving smaller operators, and a replacement property buyer should confirm which pattern the specific building follows before assuming a stabilized rent roll for the full remaining term. Rail access along parts of this corridor also supports certain distribution tenants that a purely truck-served building elsewhere in the South Bay could not accommodate, and a buyer should confirm whether an active rail spur factors into the current tenant's operation before assuming it is purely incidental to the lease.

sections.heading: Ardenwood and the Residential-Retail Edge
sections.html:
The Ardenwood area sits at Newark's edge and blends residential neighborhoods with small neighborhood retail serving that population, a different profile from the industrial and single-tenant office product found closer to the bridge. A diligence file for Newark replacement property typically includes:

  • Tenant corporate credit review for single-tenant NNN buildings
  • Lease term, renewal options, and rent escalation schedule
  • Confirmation of industrial versus flex lease structure for Cherry Street and Newark Boulevard buildings
  • Neighborhood retail vacancy and trade-area data for Ardenwood-area parcels
  • Seismic retrofit records for any pre-1990s construction
  • Phase I environmental site assessment

A buyer should not assume the underwriting approach for an Ardenwood neighborhood retail building transfers to a Dumbarton-corridor single-tenant property, since the two serve entirely different tenant populations.

sections.heading: Single-Tenant NNN Replacement Property and Lease Review
sections.html: A single-tenant net lease in Newark can make an efficient replacement property for an exchanger moving out of a management-intensive multi-tenant building, since the tenant typically covers most operating expenses under the lease. Even so, a buyer should review the lease's specific expense responsibilities line by line rather than assuming every NNN lease allocates costs identically, since capital expenditure responsibility in particular varies between leases written years apart.

sections.heading: Constructive Receipt Risks When a Single Tenant Anchors the Deal
sections.html: When a Newark exchange involves a single anchor tenant, the qualified intermediary's role in holding proceeds becomes especially important, since any arrangement that lets the taxpayer touch or direct exchange funds before the replacement property closes can trigger constructive receipt and unwind the exchange's tax deferral. This content describes process and coordination only; a buyer should confirm the specific tax treatment of a Newark single-tenant acquisition with a qualified tax advisor before signing.

faqs.q: Why does Newark have so much single-tenant office product?
faqs.a: The Dumbarton corridor's history includes a large single-tenant campus built on the former Sun Microsystems site, and that anchor pattern has shaped how much of Newark's commercial market pivots around one tenant rather than a diversified multi-tenant base.

faqs.q: What should I review before buying a single-tenant NNN building in Newark?
faqs.a: Review the tenant's corporate credit and lease term as closely as the building itself, since the entire income stream depends on that tenant's continued occupancy rather than a spread of leases across multiple tenants.

faqs.q: Are Cherry Street and Newark Boulevard buildings all the same lease structure?
faqs.a: No. Some are long-term single-tenant industrial, others are shorter flex space serving smaller operators, and confirming which pattern applies to a specific building matters before assuming a stabilized rent roll.

faqs.q: Does an Ardenwood retail parcel underwrite like a Dumbarton-corridor office building?
faqs.a: No. Ardenwood serves a residential neighborhood retail trade area, a different tenant population from the single-tenant office and industrial product closer to the bridge, and each should be underwritten separately.

faqs.q: What is constructive receipt, and why does it matter in a single-tenant Newark deal?
faqs.a: Constructive receipt occurs if the taxpayer is able to touch or direct exchange funds before the replacement property closes, which can unwind the exchange's tax deferral, so the qualified intermediary's control over proceeds matters especially in single-tenant transactions.
